subject: Operations
title: Communication Across Cultures
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Communication Across Cultures.

hook.text: A US manager asks a Japanese supplier if a deadline is realistic. They say yes—meaning it's impossible. Culture gap.

buildup.text: High-context cultures like Japan communicate indirectly. Low-context cultures like the US communicate explicitly.

discovery.text: Misunderstanding indirect communication leads to missed deadlines, quality issues, and broken trust between partners.

twist.text: Email makes it worse—tone and context are lost. A message meant as polite can read as demanding across cultures.

climax.text: Companies that train managers in cross-cultural communication reduce costly misunderstandings by up to 50%.

punchline.text: What's said isn't always what's meant. Learn the culture.

quiz.question: What is a high-context culture?
options: One that uses only written communication
One that communicates indirectly with implied meaning
